ov: The common cuckoo, a slender grey bird that looks like a sparrowhawk in flight. It summers in Europe and Asia and winters in Africa. It is a brood parasite: the female lays her eggs in other birds’ nests, each matching the host’s eggs.
wt: Males about 130 g, females about 110 g
rg: Breeds across Europe and Asia; winters in Africa and South Asia.
df: Insects, especially hairy caterpillars that many birds avoid.
fx: A female may visit up to 50 nests in one breeding season.
Most of the 150 species in the cuckoo family raise their own young.
